about.title: Lemon Grove Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, but the aftermath in Lemon Grove often lingers — a torn ligament, a fractured wrist, a concussion from a wet floor near Massachusetts Avenue or an uneven walkway off Lemon Grove Avenue. Under California law, a property owner isn't automatically responsible just because someone got hurt; you generally have to show the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn people. That's why what happens in the minutes and days after a fall matters so much — photos of the spill or crack, names of witnesses, and a written incident report can shape the entire claim. Our team handles these claims directly: we can evaluate the notice evidence, request surveillance footage before it's erased, and manage communication with the property owner's insurer while you focus on healing.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to Us About a Lemon Grove Fall

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. We know how to gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to build that case.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having nothing.

items.title: Your Own Fault Doesn't End the Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly distracted or not watching your step, you may still recover a share of damages reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Lemon Grove?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit in California. If the property involved is government-owned, such as a public sidewalk or a city building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early administrative claim. It's worth having an attorney check which timeline applies as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I fell at a store near a busy road like SR-94 or Broadway and no one saw it?
items.answer: A lack of witnesses doesn't necessarily end your claim, but it does make documentation more important. Taking photos of the hazard, checking for nearby security cameras, and reporting the fall to management right away all help establish what happened.

items.question: Do you charge anything for a consultation?
items.answer: No. Our team offers free consultations, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. You can reach out to discuss your situation without any upfront cost.
